variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Predicted consequence from the batch HGVS: NP_000220.1:p.(Trp99Arg). The papers describe the disease as autosomal recessive and caused by loss of LCAT function; the review also notes an intermediate (co-dominant) biochemical phenotype in heterozygous carriers.

quotes.quote: LCAT deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive disease [4, 5].
Loss of LCAT function causes decreased maturation of HDL particles and increased HDL levels of unesterified cholesterol and phosphatidylcholine.

carriers of one mutant LCAT allele show an intermediate biochemical phenotype between homozygous carriers and controls, suggesting that the disease, which is reported as recessive, is indeed co-dominant for the biochemical phenotype.

concerns: The variant appears only in a summary row of a systematic review table (34256778) without a case description; data are second-hand from the cited case report.
A second LCAT variant (c.802C>T) is listed; zygosity and phase not reported.
The cited reference [94] describes two patients while the row has sample size 1; the two variants may not be in the same person.
notes_for_panel: Pakistani woman with FLD, listed with c.802C>T (exon 6) and c.295T>C (exon 2), zygosity and phase not stated. Reference [94] is Charlton-Menys et al. 2007, 'Molecular characterization of two patients with severe LCAT deficiency': if that is the source, the two variants could belong to two different patients rather than one compound heterozygote; the row says sample size 1. c.802C>T also appears in the Greek and Dutch rows.
